title: to_dict returns signing_secret, so the list endpoint hands the secret back on every GET
what_is_wrong: list_webhook_endpoints serialises each endpoint with to_dict, which includes signing_secret, so the HMAC key is readable at any time by anyone with a session token.

title: deliveries endpoint is not scoped to the caller's org
what_is_wrong: the query filters only on WebhookDelivery.endpoint_id taken from the path, so any authenticated user can enumerate delivery rows belonging to another organization's endpoints.

title: no SSRF guard on the registered host
what_is_wrong: the URL is accepted after a scheme/netloc check only, so a customer can register http://127.0.0.1/, http://169.254.169.254/ or an internal DNS name and have the worker POST to it from inside the network.

title: scheme check accepts http:// and any scheme with an http prefix
what_is_wrong: `parsed.scheme.startswith("http")` is true for `http`, `httpx` and `httpfoo`, so plaintext and bogus schemes pass validation.

title: limit has a lower bound but no upper bound
what_is_wrong: `Query(50, ge=1)` allows `?limit=100000000`, letting a client pull an unbounded number of delivery rows in one request.

title: event_types is stored without validation against known event types
what_is_wrong: the list from the request body is written straight to the JSONB column, so typos or arbitrary strings are persisted and silently never match any dispatched event.

title: organizations.webhooks_enabled is never consulted
what_is_wrong: the migration adds the per-org feature flag but endpoint creation ignores it, so orgs with the feature off can still register endpoints.

title: url field has no length or format constraint
what_is_wrong: `url: str` accepts a megabyte-long string which is stored in a TEXT column and later logged and used as a request target.

title: endpoint listing has no pagination or limit
what_is_wrong: `.all()` returns every endpoint row for the org, so response size grows without bound.

title: no cap on endpoints per org and no duplicate-URL check
what_is_wrong: nothing stops a client from creating unlimited identical endpoints, each of which multiplies outbound fan-out per event.

title: no route to deactivate, delete, or rotate an endpoint
what_is_wrong: only create and read routes are added, so the `active` flag is unreachable and a leaked signing secret can never be rotated.

title: response body is built from the flushed-but-uncommitted row
what_is_wrong: `to_dict()` is evaluated inside the session scope after `flush()`, so the 201 payload is produced before the transaction commits and a commit failure still yields a serialised endpoint.

title: webhook rows are enqueued in a separate transaction from the event insert
what_is_wrong: the event's `session_scope` has already committed when `enqueue_for_event` opens its own session, so a failure between the two leaves a persisted event with no delivery rows.

title: enqueue failure is swallowed as a warning
what_is_wrong: `except Exception` logs and continues, so a broken enqueue silently drops the webhook for that event while the docs promise at-least-once delivery.

title: hardcoded three-type allowlist contradicts the empty-event_types contract
what_is_wrong: only `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed` and `subscription.updated` reach the webhook path, so an endpoint with empty `event_types` receives nothing for any other event the system emits.

title: webhooks_enabled is not checked before enqueueing
what_is_wrong: the org-level flag added by the migration is never read, so deliveries are created for orgs where webhooks are meant to be off.

title: webhook enqueue runs inline in the caller's request path
what_is_wrong: `await webhook_delivery.enqueue_for_event(...)` performs a synchronous endpoint query and insert before `dispatch` returns, adding fan-out cost to whatever produced the event.

title: an exception from any in-process subscriber prevents the webhook enqueue
what_is_wrong: the unguarded `for subscriber ...: await subscriber(envelope)` loop sits before the webhook block, so one failing subscriber cancels webhook delivery for the event.

title: the delivered body is the bare envelope payload with no event id or type
what_is_wrong: only `envelope.payload` is passed through to the delivery row and then POSTed, so receivers cannot deduplicate on `event_id` as the docs instruct because it is not in the body.

title: the signature is computed over different bytes than the request body
what_is_wrong: `sign()` HMACs `json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True)` while the request is sent with `client.post(json=...)`, whose serialisation differs in key order and separators, so a receiver hashing the raw body never reproduces the signature.

title: blocking time.sleep inside an async coroutine
what_is_wrong: `time.sleep(delay)` stalls the whole event loop for up to 16 seconds, freezing every other delivery in the gathered batch and the worker's polling.

title: ORM rows are returned after their session is closed
what_is_wrong: the rows are fetched inside `with session_scope()` and returned, so every later attribute read in `deliver` touches a detached instance and raises DetachedInstanceError.

title: endpoint is loaded and then used outside its session
what_is_wrong: `endpoint = session.get(...)` is the only statement in the `with` block, so `endpoint.signing_secret` and `endpoint.url` in `send_once` are read from a detached instance.

title: the lock is a non-atomic get-then-set
what_is_wrong: two workers that both see an empty `LOCK_KEY` will both `set` it and both proceed, so the mutual exclusion the design relies on does not hold.

title: SET and EXPIRE are separate commands
what_is_wrong: if the process dies between them the key has no TTL, and all webhook delivery stops permanently until someone deletes the key by hand.

title: the lock is deleted without an ownership check
what_is_wrong: the `finally` block calls `redis_client.delete(LOCK_KEY)` unconditionally, so a worker whose 60s TTL already expired deletes the lock now held by a different worker.

title: 60s TTL is shorter than a batch's worst-case runtime
what_is_wrong: 100 deliveries with 30s timeouts and 2+4+8+16s sleeps far exceed 60s, so the lock expires mid-batch and a second worker starts processing the same table.

title: claim query has no row locking
what_is_wrong: the SELECT has no `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and the status update is not conditional, so concurrent workers or instances select the same pending rows and deliver them twice.

title: rows set to in_flight are never returned to pending
what_is_wrong: nothing resets `in_flight` after a crash, cancellation, or unhandled exception, and no reaper exists, so those deliveries are excluded from the pending filter forever.

title: retry state is kept only in a local variable
what_is_wrong: `attempt` is incremented in memory and `attempts`/`next_attempt_at` are written only by `_finish`, so a restart mid-retry loses all attempt history and the row's scheduled time.

title: 4xx responses are retried
what_is_wrong: the loop retries every non-2xx status until MAX_ATTEMPTS, so a permanent 400 or 404 costs five attempts instead of stopping immediately as documented.

title: backoff has no jitter
what_is_wrong: `timedelta(seconds=BASE_DELAY_SECONDS**attempt)` is fully deterministic, so all deliveries failing at the same moment retry in lockstep.

title: naive datetime written into a timezone-aware column
what_is_wrong: `next_attempt_at=datetime.utcnow()` produces a naive value while `_claim_batch` compares against `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, mixing naive and aware datetimes.

title: the fetched row is used without a None check
what_is_wrong: `session.get(...)` returns None for a deleted delivery and the next line assigns `row.status`, raising AttributeError inside the finalisation path.

title: only httpx.HTTPError is caught
what_is_wrong: any other failure — serialisation TypeError, DetachedInstanceError, DB error from `_finish` — escapes the loop, leaving the row `in_flight` with no terminal status.

title: asyncio.gather without return_exceptions
what_is_wrong: the first delivery to raise propagates out of `gather`, out of the `try`, and terminates the worker's `while True` loop entirely.

title: `batch` can be referenced before assignment
what_is_wrong: if `_claim_batch()` raises, the `finally` runs and the exception propagates, but on any path where the exception is handled upstream the trailing `if not batch` reads an unbound local.

title: follow_redirects=True on outbound customer requests
what_is_wrong: the client follows 3xx responses, so a registered public URL can redirect the signed payload to an internal host or downgrade it to plaintext http.

title: the HMAC signature is written to the application log
what_is_wrong: `log.info("POST %s headers=%s", endpoint.url, headers)` logs the full header dict at INFO on every attempt, exposing the signature (and any credentials embedded in the URL) to log storage.

title: the remote response body is stored unbounded
what_is_wrong: `response.text` from an untrusted endpoint is written straight into `response_body`, so a hostile receiver can persist arbitrarily large content per attempt.

title: endpoint.active is not re-checked at send time
what_is_wrong: activity is filtered only when the row is enqueued, so an endpoint deactivated afterwards still receives every already-queued delivery.

title: no bound on concurrent outbound requests
what_is_wrong: `asyncio.gather` fires all 100 batch deliveries at once, with no per-host or global concurrency limit.

title: the loop busy-spins whenever the batch is non-empty
what_is_wrong: `await asyncio.sleep(poll_interval)` is only reached when `batch` is falsy, so a non-empty batch immediately re-enters the lock/claim cycle with no pause.

title: declared async but performs only blocking work
what_is_wrong: there is no `await` in the body, so the endpoint query and inserts block the event loop while pretending to be awaitable.

title: the returned count is computed before the insert is durable
what_is_wrong: `return len(rows)` runs before the session commits, so callers are told rows were enqueued even when the flush or commit subsequently fails.

title: permanent failure has no side effect beyond the row status
what_is_wrong: reaching `failed_permanent` neither notifies anyone nor deactivates a consistently failing endpoint, so dead endpoints are retried five times per event forever.

title: no cancellation or shutdown handling
what_is_wrong: `while True` has no `asyncio.CancelledError` path, so a shutdown during a batch abandons rows in `in_flight` and leaves the redis lock behind.

title: the signing secret comes from the non-cryptographic random module
what_is_wrong: `random.choice` uses a Mersenne Twister seeded from process state, so observing a few generated secrets allows the remaining ones to be predicted.

title: signature comparison is not constant time
what_is_wrong: `expected == signature` short-circuits on the first differing byte, leaking the correct digest through timing while the docs tell customers to use a constant-time comparison.

title: the timestamp is not covered by the MAC
what_is_wrong: the HMAC input is only the serialised payload, so an attacker replaying a captured request can rewrite `X-Acme-Timestamp` freely and the documented five-minute replay window provides no protection.

title: verify ignores the timestamp the caller received
what_is_wrong: it recomputes a fresh timestamp from `time.time()` and discards it, so it cannot enforce any freshness window and accepts an arbitrarily old signature.

title: json.dumps raises on non-JSON-native payload values
what_is_wrong: payloads containing datetimes, Decimals, or UUIDs raise TypeError with no `default=` handler, and that exception is not among the errors `deliver` catches.

title: SECRET_BYTES names a character count, not bytes
what_is_wrong: the constant is used as the length of an alphanumeric string, so the entropy is 32 characters over a 62-symbol alphabet rather than the 32 bytes the name claims.

title: the status values the code writes are not the ones the schema allows
what_is_wrong: `_finish` writes `failed_permanent` and `STATUSES` declares it, while the migration's CHECK constraint allows only `failed`, so every permanent failure raises a constraint violation.

title: model declares timezone-aware columns while the migration creates naive ones
what_is_wrong: `DateTime(timezone=True)` maps to `timestamptz` but the SQL uses bare `TIMESTAMP`, so offsets are dropped on write and reads come back naive.

title: the signing secret is stored in plaintext
what_is_wrong: the column holds the raw HMAC key with no encryption or hashing, so any database dump or read-only replica access yields every customer's secret.

title: the STATUSES tuple is declared but never used
what_is_wrong: nothing validates assignments against it, so `status` accepts any string up to 20 characters at the ORM layer.

title: updated_at has a default but no onupdate
what_is_wrong: only `_finish` sets it explicitly, so status changes made anywhere else (such as the `in_flight` transition in `_claim_batch`) leave a stale timestamp.

title: the full event payload is copied per endpoint with no retention bound
what_is_wrong: each delivery row stores its own JSONB copy of the event body, so an org with several endpoints multiplies retention of potentially sensitive payload data indefinitely.

title: event_id is a bare BigInteger with no foreign key
what_is_wrong: nothing ties a delivery to the events table, so deletion of an event leaves orphaned delivery rows and the dedupe key the docs advertise is unenforced on our side.

title: to_dict omits created_at although the API orders by it
what_is_wrong: `list_deliveries` sorts by `created_at.desc()` but never returns it, so clients cannot tell when an attempt happened or page through results.

title: UNIQUE index on event_id alone breaks multi-endpoint fan-out
what_is_wrong: `enqueue_for_event` inserts one row per active endpoint for the same `event_id`, so any org with two or more endpoints hits a unique violation and gets no deliveries at all.

title: the CHECK constraint omits the status the code writes
what_is_wrong: the allowed set is `('pending','in_flight','delivered','failed')` while `delivery._finish` writes `failed_permanent`.

title: timestamps are created without time zone
what_is_wrong: `created_at`, `next_attempt_at` and `updated_at` are `TIMESTAMP`, so the aware values the code produces are stored with their offset discarded and compared against `now()` in the server's local zone.

title: a new NOT NULL flag column is added that no code reads
what_is_wrong: the ALTER TABLE introduces `webhooks_enabled DEFAULT FALSE`, but neither the dispatcher nor the API consults it, so the flag is dead and the feature is on for everyone.

title: the organizations ALTER shares a transaction with the table creates
what_is_wrong: the ALTER takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on a hot table for the duration of the whole migration transaction, blocking all reads and writes to organizations.

title: no index supports the claim query's ordering
what_is_wrong: `_claim_batch` filters on status and orders by `next_attempt_at`, but only a single-column index on `status` exists, so the sort is done on the whole pending set.

title: no index supports the deliveries listing query
what_is_wrong: `list_deliveries` filters on `endpoint_id` and orders by `created_at desc` with neither column indexed, so the listing scans the deliveries table.

title: no uniqueness on (org_id, url)
what_is_wrong: the same URL can be registered repeatedly for one org, causing duplicate POSTs of every event to the same receiver.

title: no rollback path is provided
what_is_wrong: the migration creates two tables and alters a third with no down section, so a failed deploy has to be reversed by hand.

title: the test captures the body and the signature but never checks one against the other
what_is_wrong: it asserts only that the header starts with `sha256=`, so the mismatch between the signed bytes and the transmitted bytes passes unnoticed even though both are captured.

title: the round-trip test is tautological
what_is_wrong: `verify` calls `sign` internally, so the assertion holds for any implementation of `sign` and pins nothing about the on-the-wire format.

title: the retry and worker logic has no tests
what_is_wrong: `deliver`, `_claim_batch`, `_acquire_lock`, `_finish` and `run_worker` — where the retries, locking and status transitions live — are never exercised, only the two pure helpers and `send_once`.

title: the new API routes are untested
what_is_wrong: nothing covers `create_webhook_endpoint`, `list_webhook_endpoints` or `list_deliveries`, so the URL validation and the missing org scoping are unexercised.

title: the test asserts a constant against a literal
what_is_wrong: `assert MAX_ATTEMPTS == 5` restates the source line it imports and cannot fail for any behavioural reason.

title: the test pins exact delays and so forbids the documented jitter
what_is_wrong: parametrising `(1,2),(2,4),(3,8),(4,16)` with exact equality means adding the jitter the docs promise turns the test red.

title: the secret test checks shape only
what_is_wrong: prefix and length assertions pass equally for a CSPRNG and for a constant string, so nothing detects the use of `random`.

title: hand-rolled stand-ins replace the ORM models under test
what_is_wrong: using plain classes with class attributes means the detached-instance behaviour, column types, and JSONB round-tripping of the real models are never exercised.

title: no test asserts the statuses the code writes are accepted by the schema
what_is_wrong: nothing inserts a `failed_permanent` row, so the CHECK-constraint mismatch survives a green suite.

title: the test asserts httpx's own behaviour, not the code's
what_is_wrong: `send_once` contains no error handling, so the test only confirms that MockTransport's raised `ConnectError` travels up an `await`.

title: the documented URL restriction is not what the code enforces
what_is_wrong: the validator accepts any scheme beginning with `http`, so plaintext endpoints are registrable despite the stated https-only rule.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "it cannot be read back afterwards"
title: the documented secrecy guarantee is false
what_is_wrong: `GET /v1/settings/webhook-endpoints` returns `signing_secret` for every endpoint.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "a 4xx is permanent and we stop immediately"
title: the documented 4xx behaviour contradicts the retry loop
what_is_wrong: `deliver` retries every non-2xx status up to MAX_ATTEMPTS.

title: the documented signing input does not match sign()
what_is_wrong: `sign` HMACs a re-serialised, key-sorted JSON string with no timestamp prefix, so a customer following the docs will never reproduce our signature.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "reject requests whose timestamp is more than five minutes old"
title: the documented replay defence cannot work
what_is_wrong: because the timestamp is outside the MAC, an attacker replaying a captured body can set the header to the current time and still pass verification.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "returns the most recent attempts for an endpoint belonging to your organization"
title: the documented ownership scoping is not implemented
what_is_wrong: `list_deliveries` never filters by `org_id`, so the endpoint returns attempts for any endpoint id.

title: the documented jitter does not exist
what_is_wrong: `backoff_for` returns a fixed `2**attempt` seconds.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "delivery is at-least-once, so deduplicate on event_id"
title: the at-least-once claim is not backed by the code
what_is_wrong: enqueue failures are swallowed in the dispatcher and the unique index on `event_id` rejects fan-out rows, so events can be dropped outright, and `event_id` is not present in the POSTed body to deduplicate on.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "we POST every subscribed event to it"
title: the documented event coverage overstates the wiring
what_is_wrong: only the three types in `WEBHOOK_EVENT_TYPES` reach the webhook path, regardless of what an endpoint subscribes to.

title: the docs omit behaviour the code has
what_is_wrong: nothing documents the 30-second request timeout, the redirect-following, the `in_flight` state visible in the deliveries API, or the per-org `webhooks_enabled` flag the migration introduces.

title: deliveries endpoint has no org scoping, so any user can read any endpoint's deliveries
what_is_wrong: The query filters only on WebhookDelivery.endpoint_id taken from the path and never joins WebhookEndpoint to check org_id == user.org_id, so any authenticated user can enumerate other organizations' delivery rows including response bodies.

title: user-supplied URL is fetched by the worker with no SSRF defence
what_is_wrong: The endpoint stores any host the caller supplies and the delivery worker later POSTs to it, so a customer can point an endpoint at 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 or an internal service and use the signed request as a blind SSRF probe.

title: plain http:// URLs are accepted although docs promise HTTPS only
what_is_wrong: The check `parsed.scheme.startswith("http")` passes for scheme `http`, so payloads are delivered in cleartext even though docs/webhooks.md states "Only `https://` URLs are accepted".

title: scheme validation by prefix accepts arbitrary schemes
what_is_wrong: `parsed.scheme.startswith("http")` is true for `httpfoo://host`, so an unusable scheme is persisted and only fails much later inside httpx at delivery time.

title: signing secret is readable back through the list endpoint
what_is_wrong: `WebhookEndpoint.to_dict()` includes `signing_secret` and the list route returns it for every endpoint, contradicting docs/webhooks.md ("the response is the only place the signing secret appears — it cannot be read back afterwards") and turning any read-scoped credential into secret disclosure.

title: limit query parameter has no upper bound
what_is_wrong: `Query(50, ge=1)` declares a floor but no `le`, so a caller can pass limit=10000000 and force an unbounded result set and JSON serialization of every stored payload row.

title: requested event types are never validated against the types that can fire
what_is_wrong: `event_types` is an unconstrained `list[str]`, so a typo like "invoice.payed" is accepted and the endpoint silently never receives anything.

title: endpoints can be created and listed but never deactivated or deleted
what_is_wrong: The model carries an `active` flag that only `enqueue_for_event` reads, and the diff adds no route that can set it or remove an endpoint, so a compromised or dead URL keeps receiving signed payloads.

title: unknown endpoint_id returns 200 with an empty list instead of 404
what_is_wrong: The handler never loads the endpoint, so a nonexistent id is indistinguishable from an endpoint that has no deliveries.

title: only three hardcoded event types can ever reach webhooks
what_is_wrong: `dispatch` gates the enqueue on a module-level literal set, so an endpoint registered with empty `event_types` receives just those three types and not "every event type we emit" as docs/webhooks.md promises.

title: webhook enqueue failures are swallowed, silently dropping the delivery
what_is_wrong: The `except Exception` around `enqueue_for_event` only logs a warning and returns the event id as success, so a transient DB error loses the webhook entirely with nothing to retry it, breaking the documented at-least-once guarantee.

title: event persistence and delivery enqueue are in separate transactions
what_is_wrong: The event row is committed when `session_scope` exits and `enqueue_for_event` opens its own session afterwards, so a crash between the two leaves a persisted event with no delivery rows and no mechanism that reconciles them.

title: a failing in-process subscriber prevents webhook enqueue
what_is_wrong: The `for subscriber in SUBSCRIBERS...` loop is unguarded and runs before the webhook block, so one raising subscriber aborts `dispatch` and the webhook is never enqueued.

title: the org-level webhooks_enabled flag added by the migration is never consulted
what_is_wrong: Migration 0042 adds `organizations.webhooks_enabled NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE`, but neither `dispatch` nor `enqueue_for_event` reads it, so webhooks fire for every org regardless of the flag and the flag's default suggests the opposite.

title: time.sleep() inside a coroutine blocks the whole event loop
what_is_wrong: `deliver` is async but backs off with `time.sleep(delay)`, so a single retrying delivery freezes the worker and every other delivery in the `asyncio.gather` batch for up to 16 seconds at a time.

title: ORM rows are used after their session closes, so attribute access raises DetachedInstanceError
what_is_wrong: `_claim_batch` returns `WebhookDelivery` instances after `session_scope` exits and commits, and `deliver`/`send_once` then read `delivery.payload`, `delivery.attempts` and `delivery.id` on expired, detached objects.

title: endpoint is loaded then used outside its session
what_is_wrong: `endpoint = session.get(m.WebhookEndpoint, ...)` is fetched inside `with session_scope()` but `endpoint.signing_secret` and `endpoint.url` are read in `send_once` after the session closed, so the attribute load fails on a detached instance.

title: a deleted endpoint yields AttributeError on None
what_is_wrong: `session.get` returns None when the endpoint row is gone (cascade delete), and the code passes it straight to `send_once` without a None check.

title: the signature is computed over different bytes than the request body
what_is_wrong: `sign` hashes `json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True)` while the request is sent with `client.post(..., json=delivery.payload)`, which serializes with httpx's own key order and separators, so the HMAC never matches the raw body a receiver verifies.

title: the timestamp header is not covered by the signature
what_is_wrong: `sign` returns a timestamp but MACs only the payload, so `X-Acme-Timestamp` is unauthenticated and an attacker can rewrite it freely, defeating the five-minute replay window docs/webhooks.md tells customers to rely on.

title: full request headers including the signature are logged at INFO
what_is_wrong: `log.info("POST %s headers=%s", endpoint.url, headers)` writes the computed `X-Acme-Signature` and timestamp into application logs, so anyone with log access can replay a valid signed request.

title: 4xx responses are retried although the docs call them permanent
what_is_wrong: The success branch checks only `200 <= status < 300` and everything else falls through to the retry path, so a 400 or 404 is hammered five times, contradicting "a 4xx is permanent and we stop immediately".

title: the status written on permanent failure violates the migration's CHECK constraint
what_is_wrong: `_finish(..., "failed_permanent", ...)` stores a value the `webhook_deliveries` CHECK allows only as `'failed'`, so every permanently failed delivery aborts its transaction with a constraint violation.

title: get-then-set lock acquisition is not atomic
what_is_wrong: Two workers can both see an empty `LOCK_KEY` before either writes it, so both proceed to claim and deliver the same batch; the check needs a single SET NX.

title: SET and EXPIRE are separate calls, so a crash leaves a lock with no TTL
what_is_wrong: If the process dies between `redis_client.set` and `redis_client.expire`, `LOCK_KEY` persists forever and every worker afterwards spins on the poll interval without ever dispatching.

title: the lock is deleted without checking ownership
what_is_wrong: `redis_client.delete(LOCK_KEY)` in the `finally` removes whatever value is there, so a worker that overran the 60s TTL deletes the lock a second worker legitimately acquired.

title: batch processing can far outlive the 60-second lock TTL
what_is_wrong: The lock expires after 60s while `asyncio.gather` may run five attempts with 30s timeouts and blocking backoffs, so another worker acquires the lock and re-processes rows the first worker still holds.

title: `batch` is referenced outside the try, so a claim failure raises UnboundLocalError
what_is_wrong: If `_claim_batch()` raises, the `finally` releases the lock and control reaches `if not batch:` with `batch` never assigned, crashing the worker loop with a NameError instead of the original error.

title: rows marked in_flight are never recovered after a worker dies
what_is_wrong: `_claim_batch` flips status to "in_flight" and commits, and nothing resets stale in_flight rows or catches exceptions from `gather`, so a crash or unhandled error strands those deliveries permanently outside the pending query.

title: asyncio.gather without return_exceptions aborts the whole batch
what_is_wrong: One delivery raising a non-`httpx.HTTPError` exception (for example `httpx.InvalidURL` or `UnsupportedProtocol` from a stored bogus scheme) propagates out of `gather` and out of `run_worker`, killing the worker and leaving sibling deliveries unfinished.

title: claiming relies solely on the Redis lock with no row-level locking
what_is_wrong: The SELECT has no `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and the status flip happens in a read-then-write gap, so any concurrent claimer (or a lock failure) produces duplicate deliveries.

title: naive datetime.utcnow() is written to a timezone-aware column and compared to an aware now()
what_is_wrong: `next_attempt_at=datetime.utcnow()` produces a naive value while `_claim_batch` filters with `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, so the comparison depends on the driver's interpretation and misfires by the server's UTC offset.

title: attempts and next_attempt_at are only persisted at terminal state
what_is_wrong: The retry ladder runs entirely in memory and `_finish` writes once at the end, so `attempts` stays 0 and `next_attempt_at` never advances during retries, making the deliveries API's "when the next attempt is scheduled" wrong and losing all progress if the worker restarts.

title: backoff has no jitter despite the documented "exponential with jitter"
what_is_wrong: `timedelta(seconds=BASE_DELAY_SECONDS**attempt)` is fully deterministic, so all endpoints failing together retry in lockstep thundering herds.

title: the row fetched for finishing is used without a None check
what_is_wrong: `session.get(m.WebhookDelivery, delivery_id)` can return None if the row was deleted by endpoint cascade, and the next line assigns `row.status` on None.

title: the entire response body is stored unbounded in the database
what_is_wrong: `response_body = detail` persists `response.text` from an arbitrary customer server, so a multi-megabyte or attacker-controlled body is written verbatim into `webhook_deliveries` and later served back through the deliveries API.

title: follow_redirects=True lets a customer redirect a signed request to another host
what_is_wrong: The shared `httpx.AsyncClient` follows redirects, so a registered HTTPS endpoint can 302 the signed payload to an internal address or a third party, bypassing whatever validation was done on the stored URL.

title: no bound on delivery concurrency
what_is_wrong: `asyncio.gather` fans out all `BATCH_SIZE` = 100 deliveries at once with no semaphore, so one batch can open 100 simultaneous outbound connections.

title: synchronous DB work runs inside coroutines
what_is_wrong: `enqueue_for_event`, `_claim_batch` and `_finish` do blocking SQLAlchemy calls with no await, so every DB round trip stalls the event loop the worker shares with in-flight HTTP requests.

title: the delivered body carries no event id, so receivers cannot deduplicate

what_is_wrong: The while loop performs up to MAX_ATTEMPTS attempts in a single pass and never resets the row to pending with a future next_attempt_at, so the scheduled-retry column and the pending-queue design are dead and no retry survives a restart.

title: 4xx responses are retried although the code only special-cases 2xx
what_is_wrong: The success branch tests 200 <= status < 300 and everything else falls through to the retry path, so a 400 or 404 is retried five times instead of being treated as permanent.

title: the backoff has no jitter
what_is_wrong: backoff_for returns exactly BASE_DELAY_SECONDS ** attempt seconds, so all deliveries that failed in the same batch retry in lockstep and hammer the receiver in synchronized waves.

title: only httpx.HTTPError is caught, so any other exception aborts the whole batch
what_is_wrong: Exceptions from _finish, from session_scope, or a None endpoint escape deliver into asyncio.gather, which is called without return_exceptions=True, so one bad delivery cancels the sibling coroutines and leaves them in in_flight.

title: the loaded endpoint is not checked for None
what_is_wrong: session.get returns None when the endpoint row was deleted, and endpoint.signing_secret then raises AttributeError inside the retry loop, which is not an HTTPError and so is not caught.

title: the delivery row is not checked for None before being mutated
what_is_wrong: _finish assigns row.status immediately after session.get, so a delivery whose row was removed by a cascading endpoint delete raises AttributeError and takes down the gather.

title: the outbound signature and headers are written to the application log
what_is_wrong: log.info("POST %s headers=%s", ...) logs the full header dict including X-Acme-Signature, putting an authentication credential derived from the shared secret into logs that get shipped and indexed.

title: the entire response body is persisted with no size bound
what_is_wrong: _finish stores response.text and the f-string detail straight into response_body TEXT, so a receiver returning a multi-megabyte body writes it verbatim into the database on every attempt.

title: next_attempt_at is written as a naive datetime while the claim query compares against an aware one
what_is_wrong: enqueue_for_event uses datetime.utcnow() (naive) whereas _claim_batch filters with datetime.now(timezone.utc), so the comparison mixes naive and aware values against a timezone-aware column.

title: an async function does entirely blocking database work
what_is_wrong: enqueue_for_event, _claim_batch and _finish are synchronous SQLAlchemy calls invoked from coroutines with no thread offload, so every database round trip blocks the event loop that is supposed to be running deliveries concurrently.

title: an exception from _claim_batch kills the worker permanently
what_is_wrong: The try block has only a finally, so a transient database error propagates out of the while loop and terminates run_worker with no restart, silently stopping all webhook delivery.

title: batch may be unbound when it is tested
what_is_wrong: if not batch runs after the try/finally, and the name is only assigned inside the try, so a failure in _claim_batch would reach the test with batch undefined were the exception ever suppressed.

title: webhook enqueue failures are swallowed, so events are silently never delivered
what_is_wrong: The enqueue call is wrapped in except Exception with only a log.warning, and it runs after the event transaction has already committed, so a database blip drops the webhook for that event with no outbox row and no retry.

title: the swallowed exception is logged without a traceback
what_is_wrong: log.warning formats only str(exc) with no exc_info, so the stack that would identify why enqueue failed is discarded.

title: a hardcoded three-type allowlist silently overrides per-endpoint subscriptions
what_is_wrong: Only invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed and subscription.updated ever reach enqueue_for_event, so an endpoint that registered any other event type, or an empty list meaning all types, receives nothing and gets no error.

title: the URL scheme check accepts plaintext http and bogus schemes
what_is_wrong: not parsed.scheme.startswith("http") passes for http, and also for httpfoo or httpx, so non-TLS and nonsense schemes are stored and later handed to httpx.

title: event_types is stored without validating the names against the emitted set
what_is_wrong: Any string list is accepted and persisted, so a typo such as invoice.payed silently subscribes the endpoint to nothing and the user gets a 201 with no indication.

title: the feature flag added by the migration is never read
what_is_wrong: The migration adds webhooks_enabled defaulting to FALSE, but neither the routes nor the dispatcher nor the delivery worker consults it, so webhooks are live for every org and the column is inert.

title: the shared HMAC secret is stored in plaintext
what_is_wrong: signing_secret is a plain TEXT column with no encryption or wrapping, so any database dump, replica or read-only analytics role yields every customer's webhook signing key.

title: the migration uses TIMESTAMP while the models declare timezone-aware columns
what_is_wrong: created_at, updated_at and next_attempt_at are TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE in SQL but DateTime(timezone=True) in models.py, so the offset written by aware Python datetimes is dropped by the database.

title: there is no index supporting the queries the code actually issues
what_is_wrong: Only status and event_id are indexed, while _claim_batch filters status and orders by next_attempt_at and list_deliveries filters endpoint_id ordering by created_at, so both do sorts over unindexed columns.

title: the migration has no rollback path
what_is_wrong: The file contains only forward DDL inside BEGIN/COMMIT with no corresponding down migration, so the two tables and the organizations column cannot be reverted by the migration tool.

title: nothing prevents unlimited duplicate endpoints per org
what_is_wrong: There is no unique constraint on (org_id, url) and no count limit, so the same URL can be registered repeatedly and each copy multiplies the deliveries for every event.

title: the model narrows event_type to 100 characters while the migration allows unbounded TEXT
what_is_wrong: Column(String(100)) and TEXT disagree, so a value the database accepts fails the model's own length expectation depending on which path writes it.

title: the STATUSES tuple is declared but never enforced anywhere
what_is_wrong: STATUSES lists the four legal values yet no column, validator or check references it, so it documents nothing the code actually applies and drifts from the migration's CHECK.

title: updated_at has a creation default but no onupdate
what_is_wrong: The column defaults to _now at insert with no onupdate=_now, so any write that is not routed through _finish leaves updated_at showing the insert time.

title: created_at and updated_at are nullable in the model but NOT NULL in the migration
what_is_wrong: Neither column declares nullable=False, so an ORM insert that bypasses the Python-side default sends NULL and is rejected by the database rather than by validation.

title: nothing in the delivered request identifies the event
what_is_wrong: The request body is the raw event payload and the headers carry only a timestamp and signature, so a receiver has no event id or event type to deduplicate on despite delivery being at-least-once.

title: the limit parameter has a lower bound but no upper bound
what_is_wrong: Query(50, ge=1) permits limit=1000000, so a single request can pull an unbounded number of delivery rows and their serialization into memory.

title: the endpoint listing is unpaginated
what_is_wrong: The query has no limit or offset and returns every endpoint for the org in one response, so the payload grows without bound as endpoints accumulate.

title: the request model accepts arbitrary extra fields and an unbounded url
what_is_wrong: EndpointIn declares url as a bare str with no length limit and no extra="forbid", so unknown keys are ignored silently and a megabyte-long string is stored in the TEXT column.

title: there is no way to deactivate, delete or rotate an endpoint
what_is_wrong: active is hardcoded True at creation and only POST and GET routes exist, so a customer whose secret leaks or whose URL changes has no API path to fix it.

title: deliveries are fanned out with no per-endpoint concurrency limit
what_is_wrong: asyncio.gather is applied to the whole batch of up to 100 rows at once, so several deliveries destined for one endpoint hit it simultaneously.

title: SECRET_BYTES counts characters, not bytes
what_is_wrong: new_signing_secret picks SECRET_BYTES characters from a 62-symbol alphabet, so the constant's name misstates the entropy and any future switch to token_bytes silently changes the secret length.

title: the documented https-only restriction is not implemented
what_is_wrong: The doc promises https-only registration while create_webhook_endpoint accepts any scheme beginning with http, so customers are told their payloads travel over TLS when they may not.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "it cannot be read back afterwards"
title: the doc claims the signing secret is write-once
what_is_wrong: list_webhook_endpoints returns to_dict for every endpoint including signing_secret, so the secret is readable on demand contrary to the stated contract.

title: the documented signing input does not match the code
what_is_wrong: The doc says the HMAC covers "{timestamp}.{raw_request_body}" whereas sign hashes only a re-serialized payload, so any customer implementing verification from the doc rejects every request.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "An empty event_types subscribes the endpoint to every event type"
title: the documented wildcard subscription is limited to three hardcoded types
what_is_wrong: dispatch only forwards events whose type is in WEBHOOK_EVENT_TYPES, so an empty event_types receives three types rather than every event emitted.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "a 4xx is permanent and we stop immediately"
title: the documented 4xx behaviour is the opposite of the code
what_is_wrong: deliver retries every non-2xx response up to MAX_ATTEMPTS, so a 400 or 410 is retried four more times instead of stopping.

title: jitter is documented but not implemented
what_is_wrong: backoff_for is a pure power of two with no randomisation, so the described jitter does not exist.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "reject requests whose timestamp is more than five minutes old"
title: our own verify helper does not do what the doc asks receivers to do
what_is_wrong: The doc instructs a five-minute freshness check and constant-time comparison, while verify ignores the timestamp entirely and uses ==, so the shipped reference contradicts the published guidance.

title: the doc tells receivers to dedupe on a field they are never sent
what_is_wrong: Nothing in the body or the headers carries event_id, so the instruction cannot be followed.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "an endpoint belonging to your organization"
title: the doc asserts an ownership scope the handler does not enforce
what_is_wrong: list_deliveries filters only on the path endpoint_id, so the documented per-organization scoping is absent.

title: the test never verifies the signature against the transmitted body
what_is_wrong: It asserts only that the header starts with sha256= and is the right length, so the mismatch between the signed serialization and the body httpx actually sends passes the test that claims to cover the signed payload.

title: the round-trip test is tautological
what_is_wrong: verify calls sign internally, so the assertion holds for any deterministic MAC regardless of canonicalization, timestamp binding or header format, and cannot fail for the reasons it appears to guard.

title: the test asserts a constant against a literal instead of behaviour
what_is_wrong: assert MAX_ATTEMPTS == 5 exercises no retry code, so the attempt cap could be ignored entirely by deliver and the test would stay green.

title: the retry loop, batch claim, lock and enqueue paths have no tests at all
what_is_wrong: Only signing helpers, backoff_for and send_once are covered, leaving deliver, _claim_batch, _acquire_lock, _finish, enqueue_for_event and run_worker — where the concurrency and durability bugs live — entirely unexercised.

title: the secret test checks shape only and passes for a predictable generator
what_is_wrong: It asserts the prefix and total length, so swapping a CSPRNG for random.choice, or even a constant per-process seed, leaves the test green.

title: the backoff test pins the undocumented no-jitter behaviour and skips the boundary attempts
what_is_wrong: The parametrization covers attempts 1 to 4 with exact equality, which both codifies the absence of the documented jitter and never exercises attempt 0 or the MAX_ATTEMPTS boundary.

title: hand-rolled fakes of the ORM models hide the detached-instance and missing-row failures
what_is_wrong: The fakes expose plain class attributes that always resolve, so send_once is tested against objects that can never be expired, detached, or None the way real WebhookEndpoint and WebhookDelivery rows are.

title: fake state lives on the class rather than an instance
what_is_wrong: attempts, id and payload are class attributes, so any test that mutated a fake would leak that mutation into every other test through shared state.

title: the deliveries query is not scoped to the caller's organization
what_is_wrong: The query filters only on `endpoint_id` taken from the URL path, so any authenticated user can enumerate delivery history (event ids, types, response codes) for any other org's endpoints.

title: signing secrets are generated with `random.choice` instead of a CSPRNG
what_is_wrong: `random` is a seedable Mersenne Twister, so observing a few secrets lets an attacker predict others and forge signatures for other tenants' endpoints.

title: the signature is computed over a different byte string than the body that is sent
what_is_wrong: `sign()` HMACs `json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True)` while `client.post(json=...)` serializes the payload independently (different key order and separators), so a receiver verifying against the raw request body gets a mismatch.

title: the timestamp is not part of the signed message
what_is_wrong: The HMAC covers only the serialized payload, so `X-Acme-Timestamp` is unauthenticated and can be rewritten by anyone replaying a captured request, defeating the five-minute replay window the docs rely on.

title: the unique index on `event_id` alone allows only one delivery row per event
what_is_wrong: `enqueue_for_event` inserts one row per matching endpoint for the same `event_id`, so any org with two or more subscribed endpoints hits a unique-violation and loses every delivery for that event.

title: the CHECK list omits the `failed_permanent` status the code writes
what_is_wrong: The constraint allows `('pending','in_flight','delivered','failed')` but `_finish` writes `"failed_permanent"`, so exhausting retries raises a constraint violation instead of recording the failure.

title: `time.sleep()` blocks the event loop inside an async coroutine
what_is_wrong: The retry backoff calls the synchronous `time.sleep(delay)`, which freezes the whole worker process (all 100 gathered deliveries and the lock refresh) for up to 16 seconds per retry.

title: claimed rows are used after their session closes
what_is_wrong: `session_scope()` commits and expires the ORM instances on exit, so the later reads of `delivery.attempts`, `delivery.payload` and `delivery.id` in `deliver`/`send_once` raise DetachedInstanceError.

title: the endpoint object is read outside the session it was loaded in
what_is_wrong: `session.get(m.WebhookEndpoint, ...)` returns an instance whose session has already exited, so `endpoint.signing_secret` and `endpoint.url` in `send_once` touch expired attributes and fail.

title: the distributed lock is a non-atomic get-then-set
what_is_wrong: Two workers can both see an empty `LOCK_KEY` before either sets it, and the separate `set`/`expire` pair can leave a lock with no TTL if the process dies between them, so the batch is processed twice.

title: rows are claimed without row-level locking
what_is_wrong: The SELECT has no `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and the status flip is a separate write, so two concurrent workers (the redis lock being unreliable) select the same pending rows and deliver each webhook twice.

title: the lock is deleted unconditionally even after it has expired
what_is_wrong: `finally: redis_client.delete(LOCK_KEY)` deletes whatever key is present without checking ownership, so a batch that outruns the 60-second TTL erases the lock a different worker now holds.

title: the lock TTL is far shorter than the work it protects
what_is_wrong: A batch of 100 deliveries with a 30-second request timeout and up to 30 seconds of in-process backoff per delivery routinely exceeds 60 seconds, so the lock lapses mid-batch and a second worker starts.

title: `batch` can be referenced before assignment
what_is_wrong: If `_claim_batch()` raises, the `finally` block runs and control falls through to `if not batch`, raising NameError and killing the worker loop.

title: `asyncio.gather` without `return_exceptions` abandons the rest of the batch
what_is_wrong: The first non-HTTPError exception from any `deliver` (TypeError from a non-serializable payload, AttributeError on a missing row) propagates out of `gather` while sibling tasks are still running, and the `finally` then releases the lock underneath them.

title: rows stay `in_flight` forever when a worker dies mid-retry
what_is_wrong: `_claim_batch` only selects `status == "pending"`, and nothing ever moves `in_flight` rows back, so any crash, deploy or lock expiry during the multi-minute retry loop strands those deliveries permanently.

title: retry state is never persisted between attempts
what_is_wrong: `attempt` is a local counter and `attempts`/`next_attempt_at` are only written once at the terminal `_finish`, so the `next_attempt_at` scheduling column is unused and a restart restarts the attempt count from the stale DB value.

title: 4xx responses are retried instead of failing permanently
what_is_wrong: The success test is `200 <= status < 300` and every other status falls into the retry path, so a 400 or 404 is retried five times, contradicting the documented "a 4xx is permanent and we stop immediately".

title: signed POSTs are followed to redirect targets
what_is_wrong: A customer endpoint can answer 307 with any Location and httpx will re-POST the signed body and secret-derived signature headers to that host, including internal addresses.

title: the destination URL is not checked against internal networks
what_is_wrong: Any authenticated user can register `http://127.0.0.1:...` or `http://169.254.169.254/...` and the worker will POST to it from inside the network, giving a full SSRF primitive.

title: `scheme.startswith("http")` accepts plain http and bogus schemes
what_is_wrong: The check passes for `http://`, contradicting the docs' "Only `https://` URLs are accepted", and also for anything else beginning with those four characters such as `httpfoo://`.

title: `signing_secret` is returned by the list endpoint as well as creation
what_is_wrong: `to_dict()` always includes the secret and `list_webhook_endpoints` returns it for every endpoint, so the secret is readable on demand by any org member, contradicting the documented "it cannot be read back afterwards".

title: a failed enqueue is swallowed and the webhook is lost forever
what_is_wrong: The event row is already committed when `enqueue_for_event` runs in its own transaction, and its failure is only logged at warning level with no outbox or retry, so the documented at-least-once guarantee does not hold.

title: an exception from an in-process subscriber prevents webhook enqueue
what_is_wrong: `await subscriber(envelope)` runs before the webhook block and is unguarded, so one failing subscriber silently drops the outbound webhook for an event that was already persisted.

title: the hardcoded allowlist contradicts the documented "every event type we emit"
what_is_wrong: Only three types can ever reach the webhook path, so an endpoint registered with empty `event_types` receives nothing for any other event the system emits.

title: the signature comparison is not constant time
what_is_wrong: `expected == signature` short-circuits on the first differing byte, leaking timing information to a caller probing signatures — while the docs instruct customers to use a constant-time comparison.

title: `next_attempt_at` is set with naive `datetime.utcnow()`
what_is_wrong: The value has no tzinfo while `_claim_batch` compares against a tz-aware `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, so the comparison depends on the driver's coercion and can mis-order or exclude rows.

title: column types disagree on timezone
what_is_wrong: The ORM declares `DateTime(timezone=True)` while the migration creates plain `TIMESTAMP` columns defaulted with `now()`, so offsets are dropped and DB-side defaults record server-local time.

title: `session.get` result is used without a None check
what_is_wrong: If the delivery row was deleted (for example by the endpoint's ON DELETE CASCADE), `row.status = status` raises AttributeError on None and the delivery is left `in_flight`.

title: a missing endpoint row is not handled
what_is_wrong: `session.get(m.WebhookEndpoint, delivery.endpoint_id)` can return None for a deleted endpoint, and `send_once` then dereferences `endpoint.signing_secret`, raising inside the loop rather than failing the delivery.

title: the endpoint's `active` flag is not rechecked at send time
what_is_wrong: Only `enqueue_for_event` filters on `active`, so a delivery already queued keeps being retried for minutes after a customer deactivates the endpoint.

title: signature and timestamp headers are logged at info level
what_is_wrong: `log.info("POST %s headers=%s", endpoint.url, headers)` writes the full header dict, putting per-request authentication material and the customer URL into shipped logs.

title: the remote response body is stored untruncated
what_is_wrong: `response.text` from an untrusted endpoint goes straight into `response_body`, so a customer can push arbitrarily large content into the database on every attempt.

title: the test never verifies the signature against the body it captured
what_is_wrong: It only asserts the header starts with `sha256=` and is 64 hex chars, so the serialization mismatch between `sign()` and the httpx-encoded body passes the test that claims to cover signed posting.

title: the retry loop, claiming, locking and enqueue paths have no tests
what_is_wrong: Only the pure helpers and `send_once` are exercised, so `deliver`, `_finish`, `_claim_batch`, `_acquire_lock`, `run_worker` and `enqueue_for_event` — where every state transition lives — are entirely uncovered.

title: the delivered request contains no event id
what_is_wrong: `send_once` posts `delivery.payload` (the raw event payload) with no envelope and no id header, so a consumer has nothing to deduplicate on.

title: the documented jitter does not exist
what_is_wrong: `backoff_for` returns exactly `2**attempt` seconds, so all endpoints retry in lockstep after an outage rather than with the documented jitter.

title: `limit` has a lower bound but no upper bound
what_is_wrong: `Query(50, ge=1)` lets a caller pass `limit=10000000`, so a single request can pull an unbounded result set out of the deliveries table.

title: the new flag is never read by any code in the change
what_is_wrong: The migration adds `webhooks_enabled BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE`, but neither the dispatcher nor `enqueue_for_event` consults it, so webhooks fire for orgs the column says are disabled.

title: `event_types` values are not validated against known event types
what_is_wrong: Any string is accepted and stored, so a typo like `invoice.payed` silently subscribes the endpoint to an event that will never fire.

title: the request model accepts unknown fields
what_is_wrong: `BaseModel` without `extra="forbid"` silently ignores extra keys, so a client typo in a field name is accepted with a 201 and different behaviour than requested.

title: no bound on endpoint count, URL length or `event_types` size
what_is_wrong: Nothing limits how many endpoints an org registers or how large the stored URL and JSONB list are, so a single caller can grow the table and the per-event fan-out without limit.

title: batch concurrency is unbounded and untimed as a whole
what_is_wrong: `asyncio.gather` fires all 100 claimed deliveries at once with no semaphore and no overall deadline, so a slow set of endpoints holds 100 sockets for 30 seconds each per attempt.

title: synchronous DB work runs inside async functions
what_is_wrong: `session_scope()` is a blocking context manager called from coroutines, so every query stalls the event loop that the delivery tasks share.

title: the webhook enqueue catches bare `Exception`
what_is_wrong: Any programming error inside `enqueue_for_event` — a TypeError, a bad attribute — is downgraded to a warning line, hiding real bugs behind what looks like a transient delivery problem.

title: the status tuple is declared but never enforced
what_is_wrong: Nothing validates writes against `STATUSES`, and it also disagrees with the migration's CHECK list, so it documents a contract no code applies.

title: `updated_at` has no `onupdate`
what_is_wrong: It is only refreshed where `_finish` sets it by hand, so any other write to the row leaves a stale timestamp.

title: the index does not match the claim query
what_is_wrong: `_claim_batch` filters on `status` and `next_attempt_at` and orders by `next_attempt_at`, but only `status` is indexed, so the queue scan sorts a large low-cardinality bucket on every poll.

title: no index on `org_id`
what_is_wrong: Both `list_webhook_endpoints` and `enqueue_for_event` filter on `org_id`, which is only a foreign key and gets no index in Postgres by default.

title: `event_id` has no foreign key to the events table
what_is_wrong: The column is a bare BIGINT while every other id here is a real reference, so delivery rows can outlive or never match an event.

title: the migration has no down/rollback path
what_is_wrong: Only the forward `BEGIN … COMMIT` block exists, so reverting the release requires hand-written SQL to drop the two tables and the `organizations` column.

title: the constant names bytes but is used as a character count
what_is_wrong: `SECRET_BYTES = 32` is fed to `range()` over an alphanumeric alphabet, so it produces 32 characters, and the test asserting `len(secret) == prefix + SECRET_BYTES` locks in the misnamed semantics.

title: `verify` takes no timestamp and cannot enforce freshness
what_is_wrong: Its signature accepts only secret, payload and signature, so the replay window the docs require of consumers cannot be implemented with the helper the project ships.

title: the shared secret is stored in plaintext
what_is_wrong: The column is a plain `TEXT` with no encryption or hashing, so a read-only database compromise yields every customer's signing key.

title: the test asserts a constant against a literal
what_is_wrong: `assert MAX_ATTEMPTS == 5` cannot fail for the reason its name claims, because it never exercises that five attempts are actually made.

title: the test pins the undocumented no-jitter behaviour
what_is_wrong: It asserts exact equality with 2, 4, 8, 16 seconds, so the documented jitter can never be added without the test failing, and attempt 0 and attempt 5 are untested.

title: hand-rolled fakes stand in for the project's own ORM models
what_is_wrong: Class-attribute stubs never expire or detach, so the detached-instance behaviour that breaks `deliver` in production is invisible to the suite.

title: the new HTTP routes have no tests
what_is_wrong: Nothing covers URL rejection, the 201 body, or org scoping of `list_deliveries`, so the API surface added by this change is unverified.

title: the secret test checks only shape
what_is_wrong: It asserts prefix and length, which a predictable `random`-based generator satisfies exactly as well as a CSPRNG one.

title: no role check on a settings-mutating route
what_is_wrong: `current_user` only establishes identity, so any member of an org can register a destination that receives all of that org's invoice and subscription events.
